parts.subtitle: An overview of the origins of the modern guitar
parts.article:
The History of the Guitar
 
An overview of the origins of the modern guitar
 
(A) The earliest stringed instruments currently known to archaeologists are bowl harps. For millennia, people made bowl harps using, for example, tortoise shells as resonators, with a bent stick for a neck and one or more gut or silk strings. The world's museums contain many such harps from the ancient Sumerian, Babylonian, and Egyptian civilisations. Around 2500-2000 BC, more advanced harps, such as the beautifully carved 11-stringed instrument found in the tomb of Queen Shub-Ad in ancient Mesopotamia, now modern-day Iraq, started to appear. The tanbur* probably developed from the bowl harp. It was different from the bowl harp in that its neck was straightened out to allow the strings to be pressed down to create more notes. Tomb paintings and stone carvings in Egypt indicate that harps and tanburs – plus flutes and percussion instruments – were being played together 3,500-4,000 years ago. Archaeologists have also found many similar relics amongst the ruins of the ancient Mesopotamian civilisation. Many of these instruments have survived into modern times in almost unchanged form, for example, folk instruments of the region such as the Turkish saz and Afghan panchtar. At 3,500 years old, the tanbur which belonged to the Egyptian singer Har-Mose is the earliest known example of this instrument. Har-Mose's tanbur had three strings and a plectrum suspended from the neck by a cord. The soundbox, which increased the volume, was made of beautifully polished cedarwood and covered in rawhide. It can be seen today at the Archaeological Museum in Cairo.
 
(B) In order to distinguish guitars from other stringed instruments, it is helpful to have a broad definition of the guitar. Music expert Dr Michael Kasha defines a guitar as having 'a long, fretted neck, flat wooden soundboard, ribs, and a flat back, most often with sides that curve inwards'. The oldest known visual representation of such an instrument is a stone carving at Alaca Huyuk in Turkey, which shows a 3,300-year-old instrument with a long neck and sides that clearly curve inwards. The name 'guitar' comes from the ancient Sanskrit word for 'string' – 'tar'. Many popular stringed instruments used in Central Asia today have existed in an unchanged form for several thousand years, as shown by archaeological finds in the area. Many have names that end in 'tar', with a prefix indicating the number of strings, such as the doter, a two-stringed instrument found in Turkestan, and the Persian three-stringed setar and four-stringed chartar. The Indian sitar almost certainly took its name from the setar, but over the centuries it evolved radically, following the Indians' own aesthetic and cultural ideals.
 
(C) Tanburs and harps spread around the ancient world with travellers, merchants and seamen. The earliest guitar-like instruments to arrive in Europe had, most often, four strings. Many such instruments, and variations with from three to five strings, can be seen in mediaeval illustrated manuscripts. They were also carved in stone in European churches and cathedrals, from the first century AD through until the 13th century. When the four-stringed Persian chartar arrived in Spain, however, it changed in form and construction, acquiring pairs of strings tuned to the same note instead of single strings. It became known as the chitarra. By the middle of the 14th century, the chitarra had become dominant, at least in most of Europe. The earliest known music for the eight-stringed chitarra was written in 16th-century Spain. The ten-string version first appeared in Italy at the same time, and gradually replaced the eight-stringed instrument. A further two strings first appeared in the 17th century, an innovation which guitar makers all over Europe quickly took up. However, this twelve-string arrangement gradually gave way to six single strings across the continent. The six-stringed guitar can thus be said to be a development of the twelve-string, rather than vice versa, as was thought previously.
 
(D) At the beginning of the 19th century, the present-day guitar began to take shape, although bodies were still fairly small and narrow-waisted. The modern classical guitar first appeared in its current form in the mid-19th century, when the Spanish guitar maker Antonio Torres increased the size of the body, altered its proportions, and introduced the revolutionary fan-braced top**. His design radically increased the volume and improved the tone of the instrument, and very soon became the norm. This design has remained essentially unchanged to this day. At the time when Torres made his breakthrough, German immigrants to America – among them Christian Friedrich Martin – began making guitars with X-braced tops. Steel strings, which became widely available several decades later in the early 1900s, offered the promise of a much louder guitar, but the increased tension was too much for the fan-braced top. The stronger X-braced top proved equal to the job, and quickly became the industry standard.
 
(E) At the end of the 19th century, guitar manufacturer Orville Gibson added steel strings to a body constructed like a cello, a combination which produced more volume. The electric guitar was born when pickups were fitted to Hawaiian and jazz guitars in the late 1920s, but met with little success until 1936, when Gibson introduced its famous ES150 model.

questions.question: The instrument found in Queen Shub-Ad's tomb is the world's oldest known version of a harp.

analyses.content: 原文先提到了“earliest... are bowl harps”，后文才提Shub-Ad墓中的是“more advanced”，时间顺序上后者晚于前者。
(Paragraph A) “The earliest stringed instruments... are bowl harps... Around 2500-2000 BC, more advanced harps... found in the tomb of Queen Shub-Ad... started to appear.”
题目说在Shub-Ad王后墓中发现的乐器是世界上已知最古老的竖琴版本。原文A段指出最早的弦乐器是“bowl harps（碗状竖琴）”，而Shub-Ad墓中发现的是公元前2500-2000年出现的“more advanced harps（更先进的竖琴）”，说明它是后来的版本，而非最古老的。

questions.question: Today's Afghan panchtar is very similar to an ancient Mesopotamian instrument.

analyses.content: 题目说今天的阿富汗 panchtar 与古代美索不达米亚乐器非常相似。原文A段提到许多乐器以“almost unchanged form（几乎未变的形式）”幸存到现在，例如阿富汗的 panchtar，这与“very similar”一致。
“Almost unchanged form” 对应题目中的 “very similar”。
(Paragraph A) “Many of these instruments have survived into modern times in almost unchanged form, for example... the Afghan panchtar.”

questions.question: The Egyptian singer Har-Mose was an excellent tanbur player.

analyses.content: 题目说埃及歌手 Har-Mose 是一位出色（excellent）的坦布尔演奏者。原文A段只提到 Har-Mose 拥有现存最早的坦布尔琴（belonged to... is the earliest known example），并未提及他的演奏水平是否“excellent”。
文中确实提到了 Har-Mose 和他的琴，但关于“技术好坏”的信息缺失。
(Paragraph A) “...the tanbur which belonged to the Egyptian singer Har-Mose is the earliest known example...”

questions.question: The Cairo Archaeological Museum contains many historic musical instruments.

analyses.content: 原文只针对那一把琴用了单数“It”，没有提及博物馆的整体馆藏数量。
题目说开罗考古博物馆收藏了**许多（many）**历史乐器。原文A段末尾仅提到 Har-Mose 的那把坦布尔琴“It can be seen today（它今天可以在那看到）”，并未提及馆内是否还有“many”其他乐器。
(Paragraph A) “It can be seen today at the Archaeological Museum in Cairo.”

questions.question: The instrument carved in stone at Alaca Huyuk is consistent with Dr Michael Kasha's definition of a guitar.

analyses.content: 题目说 Alaca Huyuk 石刻上的乐器符合 Dr Michael Kasha 对吉他的定义。原文B段先给出 Kasha 的定��（长颈、平背、侧面内弯），紧接着说 Alaca Huyuk 的石刻显示了一种“with a long neck and sides that clearly curve inwards（长颈且侧面明显内弯）”的乐器，两者描述一致。
“Sides that clearly curve inwards” 完美对应定义中的 “sides that curve inwards”。
(Paragraph B) “...stone carving at Alaca Huyuk... shows a 3,300-year-old instrument with a long neck and sides that clearly curve inwards.”

questions.question: The different instruments that appeared in medieval literature had the same number of strings.

analyses.content: 题目说中世纪文献中出现的不同乐器拥有相同数量的琴弦。原文C段明确提到可以看到“variations with from three to five strings（有三到五根琴弦的变体）”，说明数量不同。
“From three to five” 是一个范围，直接反驳了题目中的 “same number”。
(Paragraph C) “Many such instruments, and variations with from three to five strings, can be seen in mediaeval illustrated manuscripts.”

analyses.content: (Paragraph C) “When the four-stringed Persian chartar arrived in Spain... It became known as the chitarra.”
题目结构是 “development of... called...”，原文是 “When the... chartar arrived... became known as the chitarra”。
题目说 Chitarra 是由一种叫____的早期乐器发展而来的。原文C段提到当四弦波斯“chartar”到达西班牙后，它变成了 Chitarra。
题目说古典吉他的形状是修改的结果，包括由 Antonio Torres 引入的更大的____。原文D段提到 Torres 增加了“body（琴身）”的尺寸（size）。
“Larger” 对应原文的 “increased the size of”。
(Paragraph D) “...Antonio Torres increased the size of the body...”
题目说这些改变产生了更好的音色和更大的____。原文D段说他的设计极大地增加了“volume（音量）”并改善了音色。
“Greater” 对应 “increased”，与 “better tone” 并列的是 “volume”。
(Paragraph D) “His design radically increased the volume and improved the tone...”
(Paragraph D) “...German immigrants to America – among them Christian Friedrich Martin – began making guitars with X-braced tops.”
题目说 X-braced top 吉他最早是19世纪中期在____制造的。原文D段提到德国移民到“America（美国）”后开始制作这种吉他。
虽然制作者是德国移民（German immigrants），但制作地点（made in）是 America。
题目说由____制成的琴弦在1900年左右变得可用。原文D段提到“Steel strings（钢弦）”在1900年代早期变得广泛可用。
“Strings made of...” 对应 “Steel strings”。
(Paragraph D) “Steel strings, which became widely available... in the early 1900s...”
题目说在1920年代，____被加到了吉他上。原文E段提到电吉他诞生于“pickups（拾音器）”被安装（fitted/added）到吉他上的时候。
“Were added to” 对应原文的 “were fitted to”。
(Paragraph E) “...when pickups were fitted to Hawaiian and jazz guitars in the late 1920s...”
题目说一个著名的版本是由____推出的。原文E段末尾说直到1936年“Gibson”推出了著名的 ES150 型号。
“Brought out by” 对应原文的 “introduced... model”。Orville Gibson 是人名，但 1936 年推出模型的是 Gibson（品牌/公司），填 Gibson 即可。
(Paragraph E) “...when Gibson introduced its famous ES150 model.”
